status: REPAIRED. Root cause independently verified (Claude Code's own runner hardcoded source_paths=None, unlike omni_engineer's runner). Fixed by reusing, not duplicating, the existing Phase 3 context-staging machinery. 12 deterministic proof tests added/repaired, all passing. One real, live governed canary run through the actual TH3/Proposal path reached promotion_candidate with authorized source staged, zero production writes. 0 regressions across the full relevant suite (97 pytest cases + 4 script-mode files).

root_cause.summary: evolution/advance.py::_run_claude_code() called bridge.submit_job() without ever passing source_paths (implicitly None), while _run_omni_engineer() (wired earlier this session, GOD_MODE_V1 FINAL GAP CLOSURE) already threaded p.source_paths from the real Proposal object into omniengineer_harness.submit_job_auto(). So a Proposal that explicitly authorized specific real canonical source paths would still hand Claude Code an empty, isolated sandbox with no way to see them -- Claude Code was structurally the only engine that could NEVER receive GOVERNED canonical source, even when a caller explicitly authorized it on the proposal itself. Confirmed independently by direct code reading (not assumed from the CT narrative): _run_claude_code's call to bridge.submit_job() had no source_paths kwarg at all prior to this repair.
root_cause.secondary_finding: bridge.py's submit_job()/_execute() copy step, when it eventually got source_paths (via this repair), had ZERO hygiene filtering of its own -- it relied solely on authority_policy.classify()'s stronger but narrower GATED_PATH_MARKERS whole-job rejection. omniengineer_harness.py's decomposed path already had a purpose-built, lower-severity default-exclusion filter (manual_candidates/, backups, secrets-adjacent, other jobs' workdirs, etc.) that bridge.py had never reused.

repair_performed.extraction: Created mrsilent_bridge/context_staging.py: the exact CONTEXT_STAGING_DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_MARKERS tuple and stage_context_source_paths() function, extracted verbatim from omniengineer_harness.py (zero behavior change at that call site -- re-exported there as aliases so every existing internal call site and test in that file is untouched).
repair_performed.bridge_py_change: bridge.py now imports stage_context_source_paths from context_staging.py. submit_job() records a context_staging_excluded preview on the job_ledger record at submission time (observability), and _execute()'s copy_source_paths step now runs every source_path through the SAME shared filter before copying into the sandbox -- previously it copied everything under GATED_PATH_MARKERS's coarser gate with no per-path hygiene layer at all.
repair_performed.advance_py_change: _run_claude_code() now re-reads the real Proposal (p = proposal_mod.load(proposal_id), a cheap isolated disk read -- the exact same pattern _run_omni_engineer() already used) and passes source_paths=p.source_paths or None into bridge.submit_job(). Defaults to [] -> None for every existing/automatic proposal, so this is a no-op unless a caller explicitly authorizes real paths on the proposal itself. Module docstring updated to reflect that BOTH engines now honor GOVERNED source_paths.
repair_performed.why_this_satisfies_reuse_not_reinvention: No new staging/authority mechanism was invented. The only new file (context_staging.py) is a lift-and-shift of code that already existed and was already proven in omniengineer_harness.py's decomposed path -- both engines now call literally the same function object.
repair_performed.why_omni_is_not_second_class: This repair closes the gap the OTHER direction too: before this session, only omni_engineer could receive GOVERNED canonical source. Claude Code now can as well, but omni_engineer remains the free/first-class path (paid_resources_allowed defaults per-proposal; the live canary below deliberately used omni_engineer to prove the flow without any paid spend).
